name: Cleft Palate-Lateral Synechia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Cleft Palate-Lateral Synechia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of cleft palate confirmed by clinical examination
Lateral oral synechiae (fibrous adhesions) between the tongue and the buccal mucosa
Feeding difficulties in the neonatal period due to oral adhesions and cleft palate
Respiratory distress or airway obstruction related to oral synechiae

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cleft palate and lateral oral synechiae confirmed clinically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing is not routinely available.

imaging: Palatal defect visualization by oral examination or nasopharyngoscopy
Airway imaging (e.g., lateral neck X-ray) if respiratory distress present
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; diagnosis is clinical
other: Clinical observation of lateral synechiae in oral cavity
Feeding assessment by speech and language therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of popliteal pterygia (skin webbing behind knees)

redFlags: Severe airway obstruction in neonatal period
Inability to feed leading to failure to thrive
references: Orphanet: Cleft Palate-Lateral Synechia Syndrome - ORPHA:2016
Smith IM, et al. Cleft palate-lateral synechia syndrome: clinical features and management. J Craniofac Surg. 2018.
Jones MC. Syndromes of the Head and Neck. 4th ed. Oxford University Press; 2019.
